Canadian Institutions

Education & Training

Accredited programs at Canadian colleges, universities, and Transport Canada Approved Training Organizations (ATOs) and Flight Training Units (FTUs). Data sourced from Transport Canada and NAV Canada.

SAIT — School of Transportation
TC ATO

Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT), Avionics, Structures programs. CARAC-compliant diplomas recognized toward TC AME licensing.

Calgary, AB AME · Avionics · Structures 2–3 yr diploma ~$8,500–$10,500/yr
Mount Royal University
TC FTU

Bachelor of Aviation with Commercial Pilot stream. Integrated flight training toward Transport Canada CPL, IR, and Multi-IFR ratings. Domestic students eligible for AB student loans.

Calgary, AB Pilot · Aviation Mgmt 4 yr degree ~$7,000–$9,000/yr tuition
BCIT — School of Transportation
TC ATO

Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME) diploma programs — Structures, Avionics, and combined tracks. Industry practicum placements included. Graduates eligible to apply for TC AME licence (M, E, or S category).

Burnaby, BC AME · Avionics 2 yr diploma ~$5,500–$7,500/yr
NAIT — School of Transportation
TC ATO

Aircraft Maintenance Technician program aligned to Transport Canada Part IV regulations. AME licence-eligible upon graduation and required work experience. Strong industry placement rates in AB.

Edmonton, AB AME · Structures 2 yr diploma ~$7,000–$9,000/yr
NAV Canada Training Institute
NAV Canada

Entry-level Air Traffic Controller (ATC) and Flight Service Specialist (FSS) training. The only TC-approved pathway to an ATC licence in Canada. Trainees receive a salary (~$42,000/yr) during residential training in Cornwall.

Cornwall, ON ATC · FSS 12–18 mo residential Employer-paid + salary
Carleton University — Aerospace
University

Bachelor and Masters in Aerospace Engineering. Research partnerships with NRC, the Canadian Space Agency, and DRDC. Graduates enter aircraft design, propulsion, avionics, and UAV systems roles.

Ottawa, ON Aerospace Eng 4 yr BEng / MEng ~$10,000–$13,000/yr (domestic)
CEGEP Édouard-Montpetit
TC FTU

AEC and DEC programs in aircraft maintenance and avionics — the largest aviation technical training CEGEP in Québec. French-language instruction. Located adjacent to St-Hubert Airport (CYHU).

Longueuil, QC AME · Avionics · Pilot French / bilingual ~$3,500–$5,000/yr (QC resident)
Confederation College
TC ATO

Aviation Technology programs in Northern Ontario with focus on remote/bush flying, RPAS operations, and helicopter training. Direct access to uncontrolled airspace and bush flying environments from Thunder Bay Airport (CYQT).

Thunder Bay, ON Pilot · RPAS · Helicopter 2 yr diploma ~$5,500–$7,500/yr

Funding & Bursaries

Scholarships & Financial Aid

Aviation and aerospace scholarships, bursaries, and government funding programs for Canadian students. Sources verified through Transport Canada, the Government of Canada, and national aviation associations.

Canada Student Grants — Persons with Disabilities
Gov. Canada

Up to $4,000/yr in non-repayable grants for eligible post-secondary students with permanent disabilities, including aviation diploma and degree programs at designated institutions.

Federal Up to $4,000/yr Needs-based · Ongoing intake
ATAC Aviation Scholarships
Industry

Air Transport Association of Canada awards for students enrolled in aviation programs at Canadian institutions. Available to both pilot and technician stream students. Apply through member airlines and ATAC directly.

National Merit-based Apply: Jan–Mar annually
The Ninety-Nines — Canada Section
Industry

The Ninety-Nines (International Organization of Women Pilots) Canada Section awards scholarships to women pursuing pilot licences or aviation careers. Candidates must be enrolled at a Canadian FTU or aviation college.

Women in Aviation Pilot stream Apply: varies by chapter
Alberta Student Aid — Study Grant
AB Province

Non-repayable provincial grants for eligible Alberta residents at designated post-secondary institutions including SAIT, NAIT, and MRU aviation programs. Part of the integrated AB student aid application.

Alberta residents Needs-based Apply with student loan application
COPA Flight 18 Scholarship
Industry

The Canadian Owners and Pilots Association awards this scholarship to young Canadians aged 14–25 to begin or continue flight training toward a Recreational Pilot Permit or Private Pilot Licence. One of Canada's longest-running youth aviation awards.

Youth · Ages 14–25 Flight training funding Apply: annually through COPA
Wings Over Water — Indigenous Aviation
Indigenous

Funding and mentorship program for Indigenous Canadians pursuing careers in aviation. Supports flight training, AME programs, and air traffic services pathways. Administered in partnership with First Nations aviation organizations.

Indigenous Canadians Flight training · AME · ATS Intake: contact program directly
BC Aviation Council Scholarships
Industry

The BC Aviation Council awards multiple scholarships annually to BC residents enrolled in aviation, aerospace, or AME programs. Awards range from $500 to $2,500 and are open to students at BCIT, Okanagan College, and other BC institutions.

BC residents $500–$2,500/award Apply: spring annually
